question.problem: Determine the equation of the streamline that passes through the point $P(0,\pi )$ for the vector field $F(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,i-{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,j.$
question.worked_solution:
The streamlines of a vector field are the level curves of its stream function and are tangential to the vector field at every point. 

If $F$ represents the velocity field of a fluid flow, then they show the path traced out by a massless particle as it moves with the flow.
. 

A vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ with a simply connected domain $D⊆{R}^{2}$ has a stream function $ψ(x,y)$ if and only if

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}=0.
$$

Note that $F(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y\,i-{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y\,j$ is a vector field with simply connected domain $D={R}^{2},$ where $P(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y$ and $Q(x,y)=-{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y.$ Computing the partial derivatives, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $F$ has a stream function, since

$$
\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y}={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y+(-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)=0.
$$

Next, we find a stream function. A function $ψ(x,y)$ is a stream function of the vector field $F=P\,i+Q\,j$ if 

$$
P=\frac{∂ψ}{∂y},\,Q=-\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}.
$$

In our case, we have

$$
\frac{∂ψ}{∂y}={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y,\,\frac{∂ψ}{∂x}={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y.
$$

Integrating these equations, we obtain the following:

$$
ψ(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y+f(x),\,ψ(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y+g(y)
$$

where $f$ and $g$ are arbitrary functions. Finally, setting $f=g=0,$ we have

$$
ψ(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y.
$$

Finally, we find the level curve of the stream function $ψ(x,y)={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y$ that passes through $P.$
First, we find the value of the stream function at $P:$

$$
\begin{aligned}ψ(0,\pi ) & ={e}^{(0)}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\pi ) \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the streamline that passes through $P(0,\pi )$ is the $0$-level curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}ψ(x,y) & =0 \\ {e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y & =0 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡y & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our possible streamlines are $y=k\pi $ for any integer $k.$ The streamline that passes through $P(0,\pi )$ is $y=\pi .$
